source: front matter of 24 of 24 pages in docs/learn; the page map for the rest

stops.title: Your data is already CUE
stops.idea: A CUE file may contain plain JSON. You shorten it one piece of punctuation at a time, and the data never changes.

stops.title: A value can be a type
stops.short: A value can be a type
stops.idea: In CUE, int and 30 are both values. One allows every integer and the other allows one.

stops.title: Writing a field twice
stops.idea: Writing a field twice adds detail. The copies must agree, and a disagreement is an error, not an override.

stops.title: Order does not matter
stops.idea: Lines and files can come in any order. The result is the same, so there is no precedence list to learn.

stops.title: Constraints narrow a value
stops.idea: A rule in CUE is a value written on the field. Bounds and regular expressions narrow what the field may hold.

stops.title: Choices and defaults
stops.idea: Offer a short list of values, mark one as the default, and select it from the command line.

stops.title: Required, optional, regular
stops.idea: Decide for each field whether it must be supplied, may be supplied, or is a plain field.

stops.title: Definitions reject typos
stops.idea: Write a shape once, build values from it, and let the shape refuse every field it does not declare.

stops.title: One rule for every entry
stops.idea: Write a rule once for every entry of a collection with a pattern. Each entry states only what differs.

stops.title: Generating fields from data
stops.idea: Build fields from a list or a struct with for. Choose keys that stay the same when the data is reordered.

stops.title: Naming a value once
stops.idea: Use the value of one field in another. Keep helper values out of the output with let. Share them across files with hidden fields.

stops.title: Conditions and strings
stops.idea: Include a field only when a condition holds. Build strings from values. See why a condition needs a concrete value.

stops.title: Packages and the standard library
stops.idea: Import validators and functions from the standard library, and share a definition between directories with your own package.

stops.title: Project, three environments from one definition
stops.idea: Write one specification from a brief. It runs in dev, staging and prod, is stricter in prod, and refuses every other environment.

stops.title: Providers and resources
stops.idea: A provider is a struct built from a generated definition. A resource is a struct built through it. Its address is its path.

stops.title: Reading a plan
stops.idea: A plan is a diff with a legend. Learn the glyphs, unknown values, the replacement marker and the Graph line, then predict three plans.

stops.title: Apply, outputs, state
stops.idea: Apply a plan, read the outputs and open the state. A plan with no changes shows that a refactor changed nothing.

stops.title: Inputs, tags, environments
stops.idea: Run one specification as dev, staging and prod. Use a constrained field, a tag and a state path derived from it.

stops.title: Many resources from one rule
stops.idea: A comprehension produces resources. Each key becomes the last element of an address, so reordering the source replaces nothing.

stops.title: Modules, providers, credentials
stops.idea: Share one definition between instances, pass a provider in as an input, and keep a credential out of the state.

stops.title: Changing live infrastructure
stops.idea: Save a plan, apply exactly that plan or nothing, and apply it in stages. Read the refusal when the plan is stale.

stops.title: Renames, moves, imports
stops.idea: Keep the object of a resource when its address changes, and adopt an object that already exists.

stops.title: Drift: find and reconcile changes
stops.idea: Change a resource outside pravo, find the change with pravo drift, and reconcile it in both directions.

stops.title: Policy on providers and on plans
stops.short: Policy on providers and on plans
stops.idea: A constraint on a provider binds every resource built through it, and a policy node judges what a plan does.
